session_covered: US and European sessions of Tuesday 20 October 2026
intro: Covers the US and European sessions of Tuesday 20 October 2026. The 06:32 run was deferred because the US session had not closed and sources conflicted; this is the 09:00 retry. The SPI 200 move is shown as a range because sources disagree on its size.
footnotes: US indices and VIX: Yahoo Finance and FNArena agree; Trading Economics' CFD-based S&P 500 (about 7,742) was not used.
Gold: Trading Economics; FNArena shows US$4,120.36, -0.52%. Brent: FNArena; CBA cites US$108.79/bbl. Iron ore (CFR Tianjin) and AUD/USD: Trading Economics; FNArena shows AUD at 70.01 US cents.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures (December contract) are indicated up at about 8,863-8,866, a gain of roughly 0.4-0.9% (FNArena +32 points, +0.36%; Investing.com +0.88%). TradingView's quote is stale and shows -0.33% over 24 hours, which is inconsistent with the US session and is disregarded. Applying the midpoint of about +0.6% to the prior ASX 200 close of 8,816.90 (-28.83 points, -0.33% on Tuesday) implies an open around 8,872, roughly +55 points (range +32 to +78 points). Figures are approximate.

local_events: RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser speaks at the Citi Australia & New Zealand Investment Conference in Sydney (time not confirmed)
Quarterly updates: Woodside Energy, Northern Star Resources, Beach Energy, Transurban (plus the Transurban AGM)
AGMs: Bega Cheese, EBOS Group, EQT Holdings, Fletcher Building, Sigma Healthcare, Service Stream, Vulcan Steel
what_moved: Wall Street's gains came from a rebound in traditional sectors while AI-linked names stayed under pressure: the Dow rose 1.02%, the S&P 500 0.28% and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.02%, with the Russell 2000 up 1.65% and about three in four S&P 500 stocks higher. Long-term Treasury yields eased and oil retreated from a five-month high on an unverified report of renewed US-Iran talks, with the market-implied chance of a Fed hike next week falling. Health care led (a health care gauge hit a record), with banks and asset managers also firm; energy lagged with oil, and technology and communication services weighed. S&P 500 sector percentages are not available.

news.headline: Small caps rally as investors rotate out of AI
news.summary: The Russell 2000 rose 1.65%, its best day in more than two months and sixth straight gain, as money moved from AI-linked shares into small caps. CoreWeave hit its lowest since May 2025 before bouncing, and South Korea's Elice fell 32% on its Seoul IPO.

news.headline: Treasury yields ease; Fed hike odds fall
news.summary: The US 10-year yield slipped to about 5.12% as energy prices dropped. CBA puts the chance of a Fed hike at next week's meeting at 17%, down from 32%.

news.headline: Oil retreats from five-month high
news.summary: Brent eased from above US$111/bbl to about US$109 after an unverified report that US-Iran talks may restart, though Iran said two tankers struck mines in Hormuz and Houthi attacks on Saudi energy targets continue.

news.headline: RBA's Hauser speaks today
news.summary: Markets price roughly a one-in-three chance of an RBA hike in November and 56% for December, with the cash rate at 4.60%.

news.headline: ASX 200 slips 0.33% on miners and banks
news.summary: The index fell 28.83 points to 8,816.90, with BHP down 1.6%, South32 down 2.4% and three of the big four banks down 0.8% to 1.8%.

news.headline: US pending home sales hit a record low
news.summary: Pending home sales fell to their lowest level since records began in 2001.

coming_up: The US Federal Reserve meets on 27-28 October, with US PCE inflation data due the same week. The RBA's inflation report is due on 28 October, when Governor Michele Bullock also appears before lawmakers.
